question.text: Per Section 3.3.2 of Chapter 3 (Benefits of Registration and Listing on SSE as elucidated by NSE SSE), which of the following is NOT listed as an explicit benefit?

answer.text: Improved market access via a common, structured meeting ground between SEs and investors/donors
Performance-based philanthropy — SSE instils a culture of performance (Social return) driven philanthropy
Minimal registration cost — saves cost for both issuer and investor/donor via minimal fees
Guaranteed tax-free status for ZCZP subscriptions

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 83 lists the five SSE benefits — improved market access, synergy between investors and investee, performance-based philanthropy, minimal registration cost, and an additional avenue for Social Enterprises. Pages 78-79 only require disclosure of tax exemption or tax deduction status; nowhere is a guaranteed tax-free status for ZCZP subscriptions listed as a benefit. Option D is therefore the one that is not listed. The Trap: Option D leans on the intuition that SSE listing must come with a tax sweetener, but the workbook's listed benefits do not include any guaranteed tax-free status; that is a separate matter for the relevant tax law and is not promised by SSE registration. Note: Page 83's benefits list and pages 78-79's tax-status disclosure requirement are sufficient to settle the question; any donor-side Section 80G or 10(23C) treatment would need a current official tax or SEBI source to cite separately.
